## 5. Electron (M = m_e): virtual part vs Brown-Feynman (lambda = m_e, i.e. their ln(lambda) = 0)
BF Eq. (49) [theta_lab = 0, extreme-relativistic]: -(alpha/pi) b(0)/U, b(0) = -ln(tau)(1+ln(tau)) + 1.355, U = 2, tau = 2 omega/m.
BF Eq. (51) [theta_cm = 90 deg, extreme-relativistic]: -(alpha/pi)(2y^2 - 3y - 2.29), 4 sinh^2 y = tau = omega_2 2/m with kappa = -2 tau (i.e. tau = omega/m).
(the printed BF Table II deviates from Eqs. (49),(51) themselves by up to 0.1% absolute at some entries; we compare with the formulae)
| omega [MeV] | delta_V(0 deg) exact | BF (49) | delta_V(90 cm) exact | BF (51) | theta_lab(90 cm) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 17.6 | 2.443% | 2.415% | 0.360% | 0.284% | 13.643 |
| 50 | 3.700% | 3.689% | -0.261% | -0.325% | 8.157 |
| 150 | 5.307% | 5.303% | -1.205% | -1.245% | 4.723 |
| 300 | 6.468% | 6.466% | -1.945% | -1.971% | 3.342 |
| 1000 | 8.752% | 8.751% | -3.488% | -3.500% | 1.831 |
| 3000 | 11.130% | 11.130% | -5.185% | -5.191% | 1.057 |

**Direct comparison with the exact Brown-Feynman closed form, Eq. (30): see results/check_bf30.md (check_bf30.py):**
the two independent closed forms (BF 1952 unpolarised trace result; DD 1999 helicity amplitudes) agree to ~1e-18 at all
masses, energies, angles and photon masses tested.

BF Fig. 5: delta' = -U^(1)/U - 2(1 - 2y coth 2y) ln(lambda) = delta_V(lambda = m)/(alpha/pi) vs lab angle, their hand-computed curves.
Values read off the figure (+-0.15): 17.6 MeV: 8.3 (0 deg), 2.4 (15), ~0.1 (45), ~0.6 (70), 3.2 (100), 4.4 (160), 4.5 (180);
2.62 MeV: 3.75 (0), 3.3 (20), 0.55 (45), 1.5 (70), 3.0 (100), 4.3 (150), 4.5 (180).
Our values agree with the figure at forward and backward angles but not in the 30-70 deg dip; since our evaluation of
their own Eq. (30) coincides with ours (check_bf30.md), and their printed Table II deviates from their Eqs. (49),(51) by up
to 0.1% absolute, the dips must be artefacts of the 1952 numerical evaluation (or of the figure), not of the formulae.

| 17.6 | 100 | 3.19 |

## 6. Non-relativistic limit, BF Eqs. (55)-(57): U^(1) = -(4/3) w^2 (1-cos) U ln(lambda) + 4 w^2 ln(w) f(phi) + O(w^2),
